results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Cancelling a factor of coprime norm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d < 0$ be an integer such that the ring $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt d]$ of elements $a + b\sqrt d$ ($a, b \in \mathbb{Z}$) is a unique factorization domain, and let $N(a + b\sqrt d) = a^2 - db^2$ be the norm. Let $u$ and $v$ be coprime natural numbers with $u \ne 0$. results.title: Euler's theorem on even perfect numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every even perfect number $N$ is of the form $N = 2^{p-1}(2^p - 1)$ for some natural number $p$ such that $p$ and $2^p - 1$ are both prime.

results.title: Extremely abundant number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\sigma(n)$ denote the sum of the positive divisors of $n$. A natural number $n$ is extremely abundant if either $n = 10080$, or $n > 10080$ and $\sigma(n) / (n \log \log n) > \sigma(m) / (m \log \log m)$ for every natural number $m$ with $10080 \le m < n$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

results.title: Giuga number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is a Giuga number if it is composite (that is, $n \ge 2$ and $n$ is not prime) and $p$ divides $n/p - 1$ for every prime divisor $p$ of $n$.

results.title: Practical number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is practical if $n > 0$ and every integer $m$ with $1 \le m \le n$ is the sum of a set of distinct positive divisors of $n$.

results.title: Thābit ibn Qurra's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ be a natural number and put $p = 3 \cdot 2^n - 1$, $q = 3 \cdot 2^{n-1} - 1$ and $r = 9 \cdot 2^{2n-1} - 1$. If $p$, $q$ and $r$ are all prime, then $2^n p q < 2^n r$, the sum of the proper divisors of $2^n p q$ equals $2^n r$, and the sum of the proper divisors of $2^n r$ equals $2^n p q$; that is, $2^n p q$ and $2^n r$ are distinct amicable numbers.

results.title: Quantile function of a real measure
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with cumulative distribution function $F_\mu$ (for a probability measure, $F_\mu(x) = \mu((-\infty, x])$). results.title: The quantile function as a generalized inverse of the cdf

results.title: Monotonicity of the quantile function

results.title: Measurability of the quantile function

results.title: Inverse transform sampling
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with quantile function $Q_\mu$. The pushforward under $Q_\mu$ of Lebesgue measure restricted to $[0, 1]$ is $\mu$.

results.title: Edges crossing a cut
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Consider a multigraph with vertex set $V$ and edge set $E$ in which each edge has a first and a second endpoint. For a set $S \subseteq V$, an edge crosses the cut at $S$ when exactly one of its two endpoints lies in $S$.

results.title: Size of a cut
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Consider a multigraph with finitely many edges in which each edge has a first and a second endpoint. For a set $S$ of vertices, the size of the cut at $S$ is the number of edges crossing it, that is, having exactly one endpoint in $S$. Distinct parallel edges are counted separately.

results.title: 4k-edge-connected multigraphs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, a finite multigraph is $4k$-edge-connected when it has at least two vertices and, for every set $S$ of vertices such that both $S$ and its complement are nonempty, at least $4k$ edges cross the cut at $S$, that is, have exactly one endpoint in $S$. Parallel edges are counted separately. For $k \ge 1$ the condition implies that the multigraph is connected.

results.title: Tail of an oriented edge
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Each edge $e$ of the multigraph has a reference direction from its first endpoint to its second endpoint, and an orientation chooses for each edge whether to reverse it. The tail of $e$ is its first endpoint if $e$ is not reversed and its second endpoint if $e$ is reversed.

results.title: Head of an oriented edge
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Each edge $e$ of the multigraph has a reference direction from its first endpoint to its second endpoint, and an orientation chooses for each edge whether to reverse it. The head of $e$ is its second endpoint if $e$ is not reversed and its first endpoint if $e$ is reversed.

results.title: Indegree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In a multigraph with finitely many edges and a chosen orientation, the indegree of a vertex $v$ is the number of edges whose head is $v$, parallel edges counted separately.

results.title: Outdegree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In a multigraph with finitely many edges and a chosen orientation, the outdegree of a vertex $v$ is the number of edges whose tail is $v$, parallel edges counted separately.

results.title: Modular orientations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $k$, an orientation of a multigraph with finitely many edges is a modulo $(2k+1)$ orientation when at every vertex the indegree minus the outdegree is congruent to $0$ modulo $2k + 1$.

results.title: Jaeger's modular orientation conjecture

results.title: Jaeger's modular orientation conjecture is false

results.title: Context-free languages are closed under inserting letters
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $T$ be a finite alphabet and let $L$ be a context-free language over an alphabet $T'$. Then the language of words $u$ over the disjoint union $T \oplus T'$ whose letters from $T'$, read in order, form a word of $L$ is context-free.

results.title: Block of a letter
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a map $\varphi$ from $T$ to words over $T'$ and a letter $a \in T$, the block of $a$ is the word over the disjoint union $T \sqcup T'$ that consists of $a$, as a letter of $T$, followed by the letters of $\varphi(a)$, as letters of $T'$.

results.title: Erasing right letters
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Erasing right letters is the map from letters of the disjoint union $T \sqcup T'$ to words over $T$ that sends a letter $a$ of $T$ to the one-letter word $a$ and every letter of $T'$ to the empty word.

results.title: Deleting a bridge adds one component
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set and let $ab$ be an edge of $H$. If $a$ and $b$ are not connected in the graph obtained from $H$ by deleting the edge $ab$, then that graph has exactly one more connected component than $H$.

results.title: Edges plus components of a forest
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V$ be a finite vertex set. For every natural number $n$ and every forest (acyclic simple graph) $F$ on $V$ with exactly $n$ edges, the number of edges of $F$ plus the number of connected components of $F$ equals $|V|$. So a forest on $V$ with $e$ edges has $|V| - e$ connected components.

results.title: Augmentation property of forests
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set, and let $I$ and $J$ be sets of edges of $G$ that each form an acyclic graph. If $|I| < |J|$, then there is an edge $e \in J$ with $e \notin I$ such that $I \cup \{e\}$ still forms an acyclic graph.

results.title: Forests of a graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $I$ of unordered pairs of vertices is a forest of a simple graph $G$ when every element of $I$ is an edge of $G$ and the graph with edge set $I$ has no cycles.

results.title: Graphic matroid
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, the graphic matroid of $G$ is the matroid on unordered pairs of vertices whose ground set is the edge set of $G$ and whose independent sets are the forests of $G$, that is, the sets of edges of $G$ that form an acyclic graph.

results.title: Bridge test for an edge set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: On a finite vertex set, for a finite set $S$ of unordered pairs of vertices and a pair $e = \{u, v\}$, the bridge test returns true exactly when $u$ and $v$ are not connected by a path in the graph whose edges are the non-loop pairs of $S \setminus \{e\}$. When $e \in S$ is not a loop, this says that $e$ is a bridge of $S$: deleting it disconnects its endpoints.

results.title: Characterization of the bridge test
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On a finite vertex set, let $S$ be a finite set of unordered pairs of vertices and let $u$, $v$ be vertices. The bridge test of $S$ on the pair $\{u, v\}$ returns true if and only if $u$ and $v$ are not connected by a path in the graph whose edges are the non-loop pairs of $S \setminus \{\{u, v\}\}$.

results.title: Forest oracle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set, the forest oracle accepts a finite set $S$ of unordered pairs of vertices exactly when every $e \in S$ is an edge of $G$ and passes the bridge test in $S$: its endpoints are not connected in the graph formed by the other pairs of $S$. It serves as the independence oracle of the graphic matroid of $G$, since a graph is a forest if and only if every edge is a bridge.

results.title: The forest oracle decides graphic-matroid independence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set and a finite set $S$ of unordered pairs of vertices, the forest oracle of $G$ accepts $S$ if and only if $S$ is independent in the graphic matroid of $G$.
